title: Systemic over-dropping is invisible: a triage regression that empties top_n by drops now yields SKIPPED lanes (exit 0) instead of FAIL
summary: F30 architecture review M4. Before F30 a triage regression that emptied top_n via drops sealed FAIL and fed the ADR-0072 blocker breaker; now each such lane is planned no-work (exit 0) and its item is handed to the console. What remains is one INBOX_ITEM_ROUTED_CONSOLE signal per item and the operator's zero-ship guardrail (no code detector found) — a partial regression (one of three lanes per wave over-dropping while the others ship) never trips it and quietly drains a share of the queue to the console.
fix: A per-batch count of no-work console hand-offs (or the no-work lane ratio per wave) with its threshold from policy config (never a Go literal); past it, emit an INCIDENT and treat it as SYSTEM-fail evidence (ADR-0072).
acceptance: RED: a batch whose no-work hand-offs exceed the policy threshold emits the INCIDENT code and halts per ADR-0072
The threshold is read from .evolve/policy.json with a compiled default (phase-settings-from-config)
